newsitem.title: USA: Park cautions pressures on margins continue.
newsitem.headline: Park cautions pressures on margins continue.

text.p: Park Electrochemical Corp said Tuesday an erratic market and price pressures on margins had helped depress fourth quarter diluted earnings per share to $0.49 from $0.59 the same quarter last year.
The disappointing results came amid a slight increase in sales for the quarter ended March 2, 1997, to $88,138,000 versus $85,751,000 for the 1996 quarter.

"Fiscal 1997 was a strange and challenging year for Park. We entered the year with a very strong market, then the market for our products went into an abrupt tailspin a couple of months into the year, and then the market unexpectedly strengthened toward the end of the year," said Brian Shore, Park's president and CEO.

"The market for our high technology electronics materials products strengthened unexpectedly a few months ago, and our people and our factories are currently working very hard to serve this recently revitalized market," he said.
He said the company intended to substantially increase its global manufacturing capacity this year to meet the increased demand.
"Although mixed signals continue to exist in the high technology electronics markets which we serve, our current short-term market outlook is optimistic," Shore said.
"However, this optimism must be tempered by the impact the pressure on our selling prices continues to have on our margins," he said.
